sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Use this example as the model for the guided set below.

items.prompt:
Function A is given by f(x) = 4x + 2. Function B is given by the table:
x: 0, 3
y: 2, 20
Which function has the greater rate of change?

steps: Function A has rate of change 4, the coefficient of x.
Function B changes from 2 to 20 as x goes from 0 to 3: rate = (20 - 2) / (3 - 0) = 6.
Since 6 is greater than 4, Function B has the greater rate of change.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Function B is given by f(x) = 6x + 1. Function A starts at 13 and increases by 4 each unit. Which function has the greater value when x = 1?
choices: Cannot be determined without a graph.
The two functions have equal values at that input.

items.prompt:
A table shows:
x: 0, 2, 4, 6
y: -4, 0, 12, 32
Is the relationship linear or nonlinear?
choices: cannot be determined from a table

items.prompt: Classify the equation y = 2x² + 9 as linear or nonlinear.
choices: cannot be determined from an equation

items.prompt: A function contains the points (4, 1) and (11, -20). Write the function rule f(x) = mx + b.
A gym charges a $94 sign-up fee plus $19 per month. Which function models the total cost f(x) after x months?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A tank of water drains at a steady rate until it is empty. Which description best matches the shape of the graph over time?
choices: increasing at a constant rate the whole time
decreasing at a constant rate the whole time

items.prompt:
A graph shows height over time.
From t = 0 to t = 2, height goes from 4 to 4.
From t = 2 to t = 4, height goes from 4 to 6.
From t = 4 to t = 5, height goes from 6 to 1.
Which interval shows the height decreasing?
Consider the relation {(5, 15), (10, -9), (1, 12), (5, 0)}. Is this relation a function?
choices: Cannot be determined from the given pairs.
Yes, this relation is a function.
No, this relation is not a function.
It is a function only if every output is different.
